Reveal each subsequent mode only after the previous completes (progressive show → act → reveal next), matching the MSE ladder's sequential-unlock model
Keep the flagship DecodeArena as the default open mode so the primary action is unambiguous

sharedPrimitives: MobileDrillFlow — single-task drill shell: segmented mode selector + 'Mode n of m' eyebrow + one drill at a time, with each mode revealed after the prior completes. Directly fixes /practice/decode (5 stacked drills) and generalizes to any multi-mode tool

MobileStickyAction — sticky bottom primary-action bar (single labeled forward button + safe-area padding), fixes the lesson 'Next lesson' footer and course/drill 'Next' controls that currently sit below the fold

MobileCompletionState — shared done → next-unlocks reveal (score + 'what you missed' + 'Next') so completion feedback is progressive instead of inline-stacked; MSE already does this inline, extract it
MobileComposeSheet — bottom-sheet composer (textarea + anon/mood toggle + post/save) to replace the composer-first pattern on /wall and /reflect
MobileLadder — sequential-unlock level ladder (extracted from mse-ladder.tsx) reusable for any multi-level trainer
MobileContinueCard — the 'one next thing' hero (reason + cta + progress) already reimplemented in /today and /dashboard; extract to one primitive so the primary action reads identically everywhere
priorities: 1. /practice/decode — split the five stacked drills (decode/page.tsx:117-161) into a single-task MobileDrillFlow (segmented, one drill visible, reveal-next). Highest cognitive-overload win; it is the flagship daily tool.

2. Lesson page — add MobileStickyAction for the single forward control (page.tsx:289-307) and collapse 'Check what stuck' (page.tsx:229-239) into a post-complete reveal. Highest-frequency student surface.
3. /practice/mse — hide SmallThingsDrill (mse-ladder.tsx:124-134) and QuizCheck (137-145) behind level completion; extract MobileLadder.

4. /wall + /reflect — replace composer-first (wall-view.tsx:191-223, journal-view.tsx:202-253) with MobileComposeSheet, and collapse per-entry action rows (journal-view.tsx:271-315) into a single More menu.
5. /record — split SupervisionLog vs CheckinForm (record/page.tsx:72-102) into a segmented control so one task shows at a time.
6. Case picker — one tap per card: remove the student-visible Preview link (case-picker.tsx:175-182) and collapse status signals (137-157).
7. /today — reorder so the primary card is first, collapse WeakSpotsBanner to a StatusPill, and demote the quick/deep chips (today/page.tsx:118-213).
8. Consulting room — collapse the 'Safety first' card (consulting-room/page.tsx:114-121) to a StatusPill/bottom-sheet note.

9. Consistency pass — adopt MobilePage/MobileHeader/MobileListItem on /dashboard and /practice (currently hand-rolled mx-auto/PageHeader/card-grid), and extract the shared primitives above so the mobile product stops re-deriving the desktop skeleton.

sharedPrimitives: MobileInput — a ≥44px (min-h-11) text/email/tel/number/date/textarea input that wraps the shared ui/Input/Textarea but enforces touch height + inputMode/enterKeyHint defaults; replaces the ~50 raw 'px-3 py-2 text-small' and h-9 inputs across every form.

MobileSegmentedControl — a 5-segment tappable control at ≥44px for 1-5 scales (check-in workload/energy/preparedness) and 0-5 blind scoring (calibration); replaces cramped number inputs and 33px slider buttons.

MobileBottomSheet (existing, src/components/mobile/mobile-bottom-sheet.tsx) — already the right primitive; extend usage to share-email (journal), Report/Pin (wall), edit (idioms), delete-confirm (students), and status-flip (rights) contextual tools per the brief.
MobileStickyAction — a full-width min-h-12 primary button pinned above the safe area, reusing the peach/ink/hard-shadow button language, so every form has one unambiguous dominant action.

case-picker.tsx:91-97 cases grouped by difficulty into 4 long sections; 'in_progress' (Resume) rows are not pulled to the top, so the dominant task is not immediate.

Render an 'In progress — continue' section first (filter state==='in_progress' to top) so the dominant Resume task is immediate.

surfaces.composition: A single `space-y-6` vertical stack of 6 full-width bordered cards rendered all at once: (1) score header with 5 stat tiles in `grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-5` + premature-reassurance warning + 'why today' line + hint-used line (debrief-view.tsx:130-201), (2) optional ComparisonStrip (204-206), (3) optional voice 'Delivery' panel with 6 stat tiles (209-248), (4) 'Three moments, done better' quotes with per-quote 'Try this again' (250-282), (5) 'What you didn't unlock' reveal (284-323), (6) footer with 'Continue with X' + 'Back to cases' (325-343).
surfaces.primaryAction: Ambiguous — multiple competing CTAs at once: 'Reveal the missed disclosures' (primary), 'Try this again' per quote, 'Continue with X' (primary), 'Back to cases' (secondary). There is no single dominant action per screen, directly violating the directive.
violations: debrief-view.tsx:128 the entire debrief is ONE `space-y-6` scroll rendering score + 5 stat tiles + 6 voice tiles + 3 quote cards + missed disclosures + comparison + footer = ~17 cognitive units at once. This is exactly the 'enormous debrief page' T34 forbids.
debrief-view.tsx:139 `grid grid-cols-2 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-5` crams 5 dense Stat cards (label+value+hint each) into 2 mobile columns before any narrative insight.

debrief-view.tsx:133-138 score `3.4 / 5.0` is presented first with no orientation ('what does 3.4 mean?') and no 'Section X of Y' context; the score leads when the directive wants the task/insight dominant and feedback progressive.
debrief-view.tsx:209-248 voice 'Delivery' is a second dense 6-tile grid as a peer of the score — should be a collapsed/reveal secondary section, not co-equal.
debrief-view.tsx:267-276 'Try this again' retry buttons are inline on EVERY quote, mixing action into feedback; retry belongs in a per-quote reveal or a single bottom action.
debrief-view.tsx:132-200 score header also carries 5 stacked status messages (AI-not-faculty-reviewed chip + premature warning + 'why today' + hint-used) in one card.
debrief-view.tsx:325-343 footer places 'Continue with X' (primary) and 'Back to cases' (secondary) side-by-side as competing actions.

debrief-view.tsx:285-323 the missed-disclosures section is the ONE thing already using progressive disclosure (reveal button) — good — but it is buried at the bottom after 3 other cards, not the payoff moment.
fixes: Rebuild as a progressive MobileDebriefFlow (T34): Step 1 score-only ('3.4 / 5 · Section 1 of 4'), Step 2 the single headline insight (premature reassurance / missed 'why today'), Step 3 quotes one-at-a-time with a per-quote 'Try this again', Step 4 'What you didn't unlock' reveal, Step 5 voice/Delivery as an optional collapsed MobileSection, then ONE next action. Keep 'Section X of Y' context visible.
Use a shared MobileCompletionState / MobileDebriefFlow primitive so each step is a MobileSection with exactly one primary action (Next / Try again / Reveal / Continue).
Collapse voice 'Delivery' (debrief-view.tsx:209-248) into an accordion or a MobileBottomSheet triggered from the score step; never a peer grid.
Make the footer a single dominant MobileContinueAction ('Continue with {patient}') with 'Back to cases' as a quiet text link, not a peer button (debrief-view.tsx:325-343).
Keep 'Try this again' but surface it only after the quote is read (per-quote expand or a step-level action), removing the inline button grid (debrief-view.tsx:267-276).

Each doc is a button row that expands INLINE to reveal snippet + 'Open on PMC' + a note textarea + save button + peer notes (library-list.tsx:140-189).

library-list.tsx:121-139 list rows are not the lightweight MobileListItem pattern; they carry a title + licence/fetchedAt caption but then inflate on tap.

Render the browse list as MobileListItem rows (title + licence caption + single chevron) so each row has one tap target (library-list.tsx:121-139).
Wrap the page in MobileHeader ('Case library') and keep the search + filter chips as the single browse control surface.

supervision-log.tsx:125-216 the log form has 6 inputs (activity, hours, date, competency, supervisor, email) + transfer note + consent checkbox in ONE card — a dense multi-field wall with no step-wise grouping on mobile.
supervision-log.tsx:113-122 summary `grid-cols-2` (Total logged / Signed off) + form + history list all stacked = three units before the user's task.

checkin-form.tsx:70-79 the three slider rows (workload/energy/preparedness) are all on screen at once with no 'Question X of 3' progression context (the directive explicitly asks to keep context visible).
checkin-form.tsx:123-136 the slider is 5 separate buttons in `grid-cols-5` — usable but unlabeled per-level until selected, and no step framing.
fixes: Split /record into two single-task surfaces (tab 'Supervision' | 'Check-in', or separate routes): one primary action per screen.

Group the supervision form progressively (activity → hours/date → supervisor/competency → transfer note behind a reveal) using MobileSection; keep 'Log hours' as the single sticky primary action (supervision-log.tsx:125-216).
Give the check-in a '1 of 3' progression — one slider visible at a time with a next/back and progress context, or a clearly grouped single-task layout (checkin-form.tsx:70-144).
Move the summary grid into a collapsible header detail so the form is the first thing the user sees (supervision-log.tsx:113-122).

sharedPrimitives: MobileCaseCard — a single-primary-action case card: patient-quote hook + difficulty eyebrow + one Start/Resume tap target; state/stars/'awaiting review' collapsed into one trailing StatusPill; Preview demoted to a trailing icon.

MobileDebriefFlow (or MobileCompletionState) — a progressive stepper that renders debrief as Section X of Y with exactly one primary action per step (score → headline insight → quotes → reveal → delivery → next action).

MobileStickyAction — a reusable sticky bottom primary-action bar (safe-area + hard-shadow) for single-task flows (finish & debrief, log hours, save check-in).
MobileDisclosureSection / accordion — for secondary info (Safety first, voice Delivery, summary stats) that reveals on demand instead of inline.
MobileContextualNote — generalize NotesSheet into a reusable note/hint bottom sheet so the session notes and the library note-taking share one surface.
priorities: Redesign the debrief into progressive sections (debrief-view.tsx) — this is the product's actual output and the single biggest T34 violation; introduce MobileDebriefFlow with one primary action per step and 'Section X of Y' context.
Fix the session full-screen composition bug (page.tsx:126 wrapper + redundant breadcrumb at page.tsx:127-139) so the conversation is truly edge-to-edge via MobilePage.
Rework the case list to one dominant action per card (case-picker.tsx:166-183): MobileCaseCard, demote Preview, collapse status chips, and surface 'Resume'/'In progress' cases first (T33).
Unify the session 'more' menu onto MobileBottomSheet (session-view.tsx:325-373) and add a discoverable 'Finish & debrief' affordance.
Case library: move note-taking into a MobileBottomSheet and make browse rows lightweight MobileListItem (library-list.tsx:121-189).

Split /record supervision vs check-in into two single-task surfaces with progressive field grouping and one primary CTA each (record/page.tsx:59-104, supervision-log.tsx:125-216, checkin-form.tsx:70-144).

workstream: T35 — Mobile notes architecture: standardize contextual notes across lessons, cases, simulations, assessments, and resources using sheets or focused editors, with return-to-context state.
items: Simulation notes exist (NotesSheet) but are ephemeral local React state — never persisted, never surfaced in debrief, silently lost on refresh/navigation/debrief.

Library/corpus annotation is the only note surface that persists (library_notes table), but it is rendered as an inline accordion expansion with a raw textarea, not a bottom sheet — the one place that violates the sheet pattern.
Journal (reflect) is the only 'notes/reflection' surface with return-to-context (localStorage draft autosave), but it is a CSS-shrunk desktop page and crams 3 secondary actions per history row.
Material viewer (resources) and lesson Watch tab have NO note/annotation surface at all — coverage gaps vs. the 'lessons and resources' scope.
Assessments (MSE/OSCE/SCT) have no scratchpad/notes; free-text answers double as scored content, not a working record.
There is no shared notes primitive: notes-sheet.tsx (sim) and the library inline editor are two divergent implementations of the same concept.

surfaces.composition: NotesSheet is a MobileBottomSheet with two Textarea fields (MSE scratchpad + Hypotheses) and a quiet 'not scored' caption — a correct single-task bottom sheet. But the sheet's values are held in local React state (session-view.tsx:92-93) and the sheet is opened from the 'More' hamburger menu (session-view.tsx:74-81, 348-359).
surfaces.primaryAction: Send message (the chat composer) — genuinely dominant and correct. Notes is a contextual secondary action, which is fine behind 'More', but there is no indication notes exist or are unsaved.
violations: session-view.tsx:92-93 — mseNotes/hypotheses are ephemeral component state; never written to any store/API, so notes are lost on refresh, back-navigation, or finish-and-debrief. Violates the T35 'return to original context without losing state' requirement.
notes-sheet.tsx:56-58 — no autosave, no 'unsaved changes' signal; closing the sheet (swipe/tap-out) discards nothing visible to the user but also gives no confidence it will survive.
session-view.tsx:74-81 — the 'More' button has no dot/badge when notes are non-empty, so a student who wrote notes earlier cannot see them while interviewing.
session-view.tsx:249-263 + debrief-view.tsx — notes are never passed into DebriefView, so 'What you wrote is half the assessment' (notes-sheet.tsx:57) is thrown away at the exact moment it matters.
fixes: Persist notes keyed by sessionId (reuse the journal's localStorage draft pattern — journal-view.tsx:9,43-70 — or a sim_notes row); hydrate on mount and write on change/sheet-close so the working record survives the debrief.
Add a quiet saved/dirty indicator in NotesSheet footer (reuse StatusPill tone or a text-caption 'Saved'/'Unsaved' line) so state is legible.
Add a small peach dot on the header 'More' button when mseNotes||hypotheses is non-empty, so the student can return to their notes mid-session.
Pass notes into DebriefView (or at least persist them server-side) so the 'half the assessment' content follows the student to the debrief.

surfaces.composition: Corpus search list; each row expands inline (accordion) to reveal snippet + 'Open on PMC' + an inline annotation block (your-note textarea, save button, unlock-copy, peers' notes list). No MobileBottomSheet anywhere.
surfaces.primaryAction: Search / open a case report. Note saving is a nested secondary action buried inside the expanded row — not a focused task.
violations: library-list.tsx:140-187 — annotation is an inline accordion expansion; on mobile this is desktop-accordion behavior, not the 'bottom sheet for contextual tools (notes/hints)' the directive requires.
library-list.tsx:157-163 — raw <textarea>, not the shared ui/textarea primitive (used correctly by notes-sheet.tsx) — divergent implementation.
library-list.tsx:164-187 — save button, unlock copy, and peers' notes all stack inline in one cramped bordered div, giving three cognitive units at once instead of show → act → reveal next.

library-list.tsx:126-139 — the row button toggles open AND triggers loadNotes in one handler; note state and expansion state are coupled, so closing the row discards an unsaved draft (no draft buffer, no autosave).
fixes: Extract the annotation into a NotesSheet-style MobileBottomSheet opened by a StickyNote affordance on each row; keep the list row collapsed as a simple title+meta+trailing note glyph.
Reuse the shared Textarea primitive and MobileBottomSheet (mirror notes-sheet.tsx) so sim notes and library notes speak the same language.
Stage the reveal: sheet shows your note first, 'Save note' persists, then unlock copy + peers list appear (progressive disclosure) instead of everything at once.
Keep the existing library_notes persistence (api/practice/library/note/route.ts) and add a draft buffer keyed by documentId so closing the sheet doesn't lose an unsaved note.

surfaces.composition: Desktop container (page.tsx:27 'max-w-3xl px-4 py-8'), not MobilePage/MobileHeader. Write form (mood chips + textarea + Save) then a history list where each entry carries up to 3 secondary buttons and inline-expanding share/help panels.
surfaces.primaryAction: Save entry (journal-view.tsx:241-247) — dominant and correct in the write form; but the history list has no single primary and shows 3 competing actions per row.
violations: page.tsx:27 — not mobile-composed (no MobilePage/MobileHeader/MobileSection); a CSS-shrunk desktop page.

journal-view.tsx:271-314 — each entry row renders 'Help me think about this' + 'Share with faculty' + 'Share' simultaneously as text-caption px-2 py-1 buttons — three actions per row, touch targets below the 44px floor, no progressive disclosure.
journal-view.tsx:320-339 — the share-email input expands inline inside the list item rather than in a bottom sheet / focused editor.
journal-view.tsx:343-348 — the 'help me think' reply renders inline, pushing the entry content down; should reveal in a sheet.
fixes: Compose page.tsx with MobilePage + MobileHeader ('Your journal') + MobileSection so it reads as the mobile product, not a shrunk desktop.
Collapse the 3 per-entry buttons into a single 'More' affordance opening a MobileBottomSheet with Help / Share-with-faculty / Share / Revoke (one row, ≥44px).
Move the share-email input and the reflective-prompt reply into the sheet (or a focused editor) so the history list stays one scannable column.
Keep the localStorage draft autosave (journal-view.tsx:43-70, 249-251) — it is the correct return-to-context pattern to replicate elsewhere.

surfaces.composition: Full-height material viewer with a minimal header (back + title + prev/next). No annotation or note surface of any kind.
surfaces.primaryAction: View the material / prev-next navigation — correct and dominant.
violations: page.tsx:71-121 — resources have no note affordance at all; T35 scope explicitly includes 'resources', so this is a coverage gap.
No way to attach a teaching-point note to a PDF/audio/slide while reading — the exact contextual use case the directive calls out.
fixes: Add a StickyNote affordance in the material header (page.tsx:85-106) opening a MobileNotesSheet keyed by materialId.
Persist via a material-scoped notes row (reuse the library_notes pattern from api/practice/library/note/route.ts) so notes return with the material.

surfaces.composition: Desktop max-w-5xl with Watch/Materials/Assignment tabs and a single forward ContinueControl. No note/annotation surface.
surfaces.primaryAction: Next lesson / Finish course (ContinueControl, page.tsx:299-307) — already a single forward action, correct.
violations: page.tsx:168-239 — no note/annotation surface on the Watch tab; T35 scope includes 'lessons', so this is a coverage gap.
The 'Check what stuck' section (page.tsx:229-239) is the only reflection touchpoint; no place to capture a lesson takeaway note.
fixes: Add a notes affordance on the Watch tab (a header or trailing action) opening a shared MobileNotesSheet keyed by lessonId, so a student can capture a takeaway without leaving the lesson.

surfaces.composition: Assessment trainers rendered in desktop max-w-3xl containers; free-text fields are scored answers, with no separate scratchpad/working-notes surface.
surfaces.primaryAction: Submit the assessment answer — correct; a separate notes affordance is absent.
violations: No contextual scratchpad/notes for assessments; the free-text answer doubles as both scored work and the student's thinking, so there is no unscrewed working record.
T35 scope includes 'assessments', so this is a coverage gap (lower priority — scored answers already capture the work).
fixes: Add an optional scratchpad via the shared MobileNotesSheet where an assessment has multi-step reasoning (e.g. full MSE / OSCE station); keep it unscrewed and draft-persisted.

sharedPrimitives: MobileNotesSheet — generalize src/components/sim/notes-sheet.tsx into a reusable notes bottom-sheet built on MobileBottomSheet: title, one/two focused Textarea sections, autosave draft, saved/unsaved indicator, and an optional 'unlock peers' reveal slot. One notes surface for sim, library, materials, lessons, and assessment scratchpads.

NotesHeaderAffordance — a StickyNote/NotebookPen button (≥44px) with a peach dot when the note is non-empty, so notes are discoverable and their state visible without opening the sheet (fixes the blind 'More' button in session-view.tsx).

useNoteDraft(storageKey) — a small hook replicating the journal's debounced localStorage autosave (journal-view.tsx:43-70, DRAFT_KEY pattern) so every notes surface returns to context without a bespoke table, then syncs to a server row when it exists.
NoteSheetSaveState — a StatusPill/text-caption 'Saved · Unsaved' footer slot in MobileBottomSheet so the save state of a note is legible on close.
priorities: Persist sim notes and add a saved indicator + non-empty dot (session-view.tsx:92-93, 74-81; notes-sheet.tsx:56-58) — highest value: this is the only note surface where content already exists but is silently destroyed, directly breaking 'return to context without losing state'.

Extract library annotation into a MobileBottomSheet with staged reveal (library-list.tsx:140-187) and reuse the shared Textarea + MobileBottomSheet — fixes the single worst pattern violation (inline accordion notes).
Mobile-compose /reflect and collapse the 3-per-entry buttons into a More sheet (page.tsx:27; journal-view.tsx:271-348) — brings the journal into the mobile product and off the CSS-shrunk desktop.

Add a shared MobileNotesSheet affordance to the material viewer (materials/[materialId]/page.tsx:71-121) and the lesson Watch tab (lessons/[lessonId]/page.tsx:168-239) to close the resources/lessons coverage gap.
Add an optional unscrewed scratchpad to multi-step assessments (full MSE / OSCE station) via the shared sheet — lowest priority since scored answers already capture the work.

items: T32 — Mobile psychopharmacology experience: redesign medication browsing, medication details, comparisons, learning checks, and related educational interactions for mobile; prioritize one medication/concept at a time and progressively expose secondary information.

surfaces.composition: Search landing: centered single autofocused field (PsychSearch) + one 'Browse by mechanism' card-link + standing notice. Rendered inside AppShell, which supplies the mobile top bar and bottom tab bar. This is already the closest thing to a correct mobile screen in the workstream.
surfaces.primaryAction: Type-to-search (the autofocused input) — genuinely the ONE primary action and it IS dominant. Secondary 'Browse by mechanism' is correctly de-emphasized below it.
violations: No mobile primitives used; the page is a bare desktop div (src/app/(dashboard)/tools/psychopharm/page.tsx:13 `min-h-[70vh] flex-col items-center justify-center gap-8`) — content is vertically centered, leaving a large dead band at the top of a phone and pushing the search field toward the bottom tab bar.

The intended 3-step progressive flow (name → dose chips → band view) is broken: PsychSearch.pick() calls router.push() immediately after kicking off the bands fetch (src/components/psychopharm/psych-search.tsx:72), so the dose-chip 'step 2' UI (psych-search.tsx:161-189) never renders — the screen unmounts before the fetch resolves. The 'Pick a dose' chips are dead code on mobile.
The 'Browse by mechanism' link (page.tsx:24-38) is hand-rolled desktop markup (border-2 + hard-shadow-sm card) instead of the existing MobileCard primitive.
No top-level page header/eyebrow using MobileHeader; on a phone the screen has no title context other than the shell top bar.
fixes: Wrap in MobilePage and add a MobileHeader with title 'Psychopharm' so the search screen reads as an app screen rather than a floating centered div (src/components/mobile/mobile-page.tsx, mobile-header.tsx).

Fix the 3-step flow: in PsychSearch.pick() (psych-search.tsx:62-73), do NOT router.push until the dose chips resolve; render the chips, then navigate with ?band= on chip tap — restoring show→act→reveal-next.
Replace the hand-rolled browse link with MobileCard href='/tools/psychopharm/learn' (mobile-card.tsx).
Change the vertical-centering to top-aligned (`items-start` / reduce min-h) so the search field sits in the thumb zone instead of mid-screen.

surfaces.composition: Drug + band detail. One flat `max-w-3xl space-y-6` scroll (page.tsx:38) stacking: text-link back row (39-49), header (51-62), DoseLadder, then DrugBandView which renders BandDetail + OnsetTimeline + RegisterView + 'Commonly used in' + 'What to watch for' + up to 6 FDA label sections + ObserverNotes (drug-band-view.tsx:70-139). ~10+ full content sections dumped on one screen.
surfaces.primaryAction: There is NO dominant primary action. The only real interaction is the dose ladder (tap a rung → reveal that band). The 'Compare →' affordance is a 12px text-caption link (page.tsx:43-47), visually weightless. So the screen reads as 'here are 17 things' — exactly the anti-pattern the directive forbids.
violations: Entire page is one undifferentiated long scroll — no progressive disclosure. DrugBandView renders every section unconditionally: band detail (drug-band-view.tsx:70), onset timeline (73), register view (84), common uses (93), side effects (106), then a .map over 6 FDA sections (121-135), then ObserverNotes (138).
No sticky back control / context header: back is a text-caption '← Search' link (page.tsx:40) not MobileHeader; no 'dose N of M' or 'Section 1 of 5' context while the band ladder is active.
Register toggle (student/clinician) is a mid-page SegmentedControl (register-view.tsx:32-40) buried at scroll position ~3; it is a full-page register switch treated as an inline widget.

Secondary FDA label sections (Contraindications, Interactions, Monitoring, Overdose, Special populations, Patient counseling) are all expanded inline (drug-band-view.tsx:121-135) — textbook 'hide until needed' material.

ObserverNotes is one giant section with 6 sub-parts (session obs, timeline, therapist questions, red flags, pearls, checklist, vignette) all expanded (observer-notes.tsx:37-139) — a huge cognitive dump for a two-minute-gap student.
No mobile primitives anywhere: no MobilePage, no MobileHeader, no MobileSection, no MobileBottomSheet for the contextual tools.
Search affordance disappears on the detail page — the only way to search another drug is the tiny back link.
fixes: Wrap in MobilePage + MobileHeader (backHref='/tools/psychopharm', title=drug.generic, subtitle=drug.class) so back is a 40px touch target with safe-area inset (mobile-header.tsx).

Restructure DrugBandView into a single-task step flow: Step 1 = DoseLadder (band picker, keep 'Tap a dose' eyebrow + band count '3 of 4'), Step 2 = BandDetail for the active band only, Step 3 = reveal 'Commonly used in' + 'What to watch for' on demand. Use MobileSection for each (mobile-section.tsx).
Move the register toggle into a MobileHeader action or a top SegmentedControl pinned above the band content, not mid-scroll.

Collapse the 6 FDA label sections into a single expandable MobileSection ('Full label') or a MobileBottomSheet (mobile-bottom-sheet.tsx) triggered by a 'Full label' action — progressively revealed, never removed.
Move ObserverNotes into a MobileBottomSheet ('Session notes / red flags') opened from a bottom-sheet action; keep the sheet scrollable so no functionality is lost, just revealed on demand.
Promote ONE primary action: a full-width peach 'Compare this drug' button (mobile-card/button) that links to /tools/psychopharm/compare?a={drug}&b= — replacing the text-caption link.
Keep a compact sticky search shortcut in the header so students can jump to another drug without going back to the landing page.

surfaces.composition: Comparison view built as a wide desktop table: `max-w-5xl` (page.tsx:36) wrapping a `<table>` inside `overflow-x-auto` (page.tsx:66-90) with one column per drug (2-5 columns) and 9 field rows. Empty state (page.tsx:17-29) instructs the user to hand-edit URL params.
surfaces.primaryAction: None. The page is read-only; the only exit is a text-caption '← Search' link (page.tsx:37). There is no 'add a drug' or 'pick two drugs' action at all — the user is expected to type slugs into the URL.
violations: Horizontal-scroll comparison table (page.tsx:66 `<div className='overflow-x-auto'>` + `<table>` at 67) is the literal definition of a CSS-shrunk desktop — on a phone you swipe sideways across 2-5 columns and lose all column headers while scrolling.
Drug selection requires editing URL query params (`?a=…&b=…&c=…`, page.tsx:17-27) — a desktop keyboard interaction with no mobile picker.
No single concept/field focus: all 9 fields × N drugs are on screen simultaneously, violating 'one cognitive unit at a time'.
No mobile primitives (no MobileHeader, no MobileListItem/MobileCard for the drugs being compared).
fixes: Replace the table with a mobile card-per-drug composition: a horizontal drug strip (or step indicator '2 of 3 drugs') plus ONE field at a time with next/prev, or a stacked field-by-field comparison where each field is a MobileSection comparing the 2-3 drugs vertically.
Add a real mobile picker: reuse PsychSearch to select drug A then B (show→act→reveal-next), then land on the comparison — no URL editing.
Give the screen ONE primary action ('Add a drug to compare' / 'Compare another'), with a sticky continue/back control.
Keep the 'Comparing whole drugs is nearly meaningless' honest copy (page.tsx:41-44) but present the band context per drug via a small StatusPill or caption, not a table column.

surfaces.composition: Browse by mechanism: `max-w-4xl space-y-8` (page.tsx:14) list of mechanism-group sections, each a card with a badge count and a `flex flex-wrap gap-2` wall of small pill links to every drug in that group (page.tsx:26-47). Uses desktop PageHeader (page.tsx:19).
surfaces.primaryAction: None explicit — it is a browse list. Each drug is a small pill link (~30px tall), so the 'action' is tapping a drug pill, but there are dozens of them competing per screen.
violations: Dense pill wall: every drug in every mechanism group is rendered as a small `rounded-full border-2 px-3 py-1 text-sm` link (page.tsx:37) — ~30px touch height, far below the 44px primary-target floor, and dozens visible at once with no progressive disclosure.
No group→drug progressive reveal: mechanism groups are all expanded; there's no 'tap group → reveal its drugs' single-task step.
Desktop PageHeader (page.tsx:19-23) instead of a MobileHeader with a real back target to /tools/psychopharm.
Not using MobileListItem (the workhorse row primitive, min 48px) or MobileCard for the groups.
fixes: Render each mechanism group as a MobileCard (tap → push a group detail route) so the top level is one concept (the receptor group) per card, then reveal the drugs one screen down (show→act→reveal-next).
On the group detail, list drugs with MobileListItem (48px rows, leading glyph + class qualifier as subtitle) instead of pills.
Swap PageHeader for MobileHeader (backHref='/tools/psychopharm', title='Browse by mechanism').
Keep the 'mechanism, not a list of doses' honest caption (page.tsx:50-53) but move it into a MobileSection description.

surfaces.composition: Admin medication list: `space-y-6` list (page.tsx:55) of ~100 drugs, each a full-width Link row `flex items-center justify-between gap-3 p-3` (page.tsx:73-98) with drug name + class badge + 2-line summary on the left and a shrink-0 right cluster (status Badge + 'Open' + ArrowRight).
surfaces.primaryAction: 'Open' (navigate to the editor) is the one action and is correct per-row, but it is rendered as a text-caption 'Open →' (page.tsx:92-95) rather than a dominant control.
violations: Rows are desktop-flex markup, not MobileListItem; the shrink-0 right cluster (status badge + 'Open' + chevron) at page.tsx:90-96 competes with the name + class badge + 2-line summary on a 360px viewport and will crowd/wrap.
No MobileHeader/PageHeader mobile treatment; PageHeader (page.tsx:56) is desktop composition.
ReviewFilter (review-filter.tsx:27-34) is a fine input but has no mobile filter sheet/clear affordance.
fixes: Replace the hand-rolled row Link with MobileListItem (href to editor, title=drug name, subtitle=plain summary, trailing=StatusPill + label) — 48px rows, one clean tap target, status as a pill not a competing badge (mobile-list-item.tsx + status-pill.tsx).
Use StatusPill (tone=neutral/scripted/warning mapped from statusBadge) for the status instead of the desktop Badge cluster.
Optionally move the filter into a MobileBottomSheet 'Filter' action on mobile, but this is admin — lower priority than the student surfaces.

surfaces.composition: Two-pane inline editor at fixed height `h-[calc(100vh-3rem)]` (page.tsx:38) wrapping EditorPane, which is `flex flex-1 overflow-hidden` (editor-pane.tsx:125) with a flex-1 preview/editor left and a fixed `w-80 shrink-0` right rail (editor-pane.tsx:168) holding status, Publish, and SourcePanel.
surfaces.primaryAction: 'Publish to students' (editor-pane.tsx:193-200) is the one real action, but it lives in a 320px right rail that does not exist as a usable column on a phone.
violations: Fixed two-pane split (editor-pane.tsx:125 flex + 168 `w-80 shrink-0`) has no `flex-col lg:flex-row` switch — on mobile the 320px rail and the flex-1 edit surface are crammed side-by-side (or the preview collapses to ~40px), making the editor effectively unusable.

Inline block controls (Edit / Sources / Remove) are hover-only: document-view.tsx:307 `group ... hover:border-primary/40` and :309 `hidden group-hover:flex` — on touch there is no hover, so these controls are unreachable on mobile (functional regression, not just styling).
No MobileHeader back target; back is a text-caption '← Library' link (page.tsx:41).
Entire editor is desktop-first with zero mobile treatment; the right rail (status + change note + Publish + source panel) should be a bottom sheet on mobile.
fixes: Make EditorPane responsive: `flex flex-col lg:flex-row` so on mobile the document stacks above the right rail (or the rail becomes a MobileBottomSheet 'Review & Publish' opened from a sticky action).

Make block controls touch-accessible: change `group-hover:flex` to `group-focus-within:flex` plus an always-visible affordance, or render an explicit 'Edit' tap target on touch (document-view.tsx:309).
Wrap in MobileHeader (backHref='/admin/psychopharm-review', title=drug.generic, subtitle=`v${version} · ${status}`).
Promote a single sticky 'Publish' action in the mobile header or a sticky bottom action rather than a buried rail button.

items: T36 — Mobile search experience: create a phone-first search flow with focused results, useful filters, progressive refinement, and contextual result details instead of dense desktop result grids.

T37 — Mobile filters and sorting: convert dense desktop filter panels into mobile bottom sheets / progressive filter flows; preserve all filtering capabilities without permanently consuming screen space.

surfaces.composition: Single desktop column `mx-auto max-w-3xl px-4 py-8 sm:px-6` (page.tsx:25). A form-submit search input (library-list.tsx:99-107) + a row of 10 keyword-filter chips that `flex flex-wrap` (page.tsx:35-48) + a `ul` of expand-in-place cards each embedding an inline note editor (library-list.tsx:121-193). No mobile shell primitives (no MobileHeader/MobileSection); only the generic shell top bar is present.
surfaces.primaryAction: Search the corpus (title/opening text). It is not dominant — the search input, 10 filter chips, and ~50 result cards all share equal visual weight on load; there is no single focal action.
violations: Dense desktop filter panel: 10 filter chips permanently consume vertical space and wrap to multiple rows on a 320px viewport (page.tsx:35-48) — should be a progressive bottom-sheet filter.

Search is form-submit + full navigation, not progressive: `<form onSubmit>` pushes `?q=` and re-renders the whole page (library-list.tsx:88-95, 99-107); no live/debounced filtering, so the mobile keyboard 'go' is the only path.

Contextual tool (notes/hints) is inline, not a bottom sheet: the 'Your note' textarea + peers' notes expand inside the card (library-list.tsx:140-187), inflating every row instead of revealing in a sheet.
Hard result cap hides content: `filtered.slice(0, 50)` with no load-more (page.tsx:50, 61) — the rest of the corpus is unreachable on any device, no progressive disclosure.

Filter chips drop the active query: the tag link builds `?tag=` without the current `q`, and the active chip links back to bare `/practice/library` (page.tsx:39-42), so filtering clears the search silently.
No contextual result detail beyond an inline snippet + external 'Open on PMC' link (library-list.tsx:142-150); results are title-only, no way to refine to a detail view.
fixes: Wrap the route in MobilePage + MobileHeader (back to /practice) and compose results as MobileListItem rows (title + licence/fetchedAt subtitle + chevron) instead of custom `<button>` cards (library-list.tsx:121-139).
Make search live/debounced client-side over the in-memory list (mirror the PsychSearch pattern at psych-search.tsx:38-60) instead of form-submit page navigation.

Replace the 10-chip row with a single 'Filter' button opening a MobileBottomSheet; list LIBRARY_FILTERS as selectable rows, keep the active filters as removable StatusPill chips above the list (page.tsx:35-48).
Move the note editor + peers' notes into a MobileBottomSheet opened per result (contextual tool), leaving the row a single tap target.
Replace the 50-cap with a 'Load more' button / progressive pagination and surface 'Showing N of M' prominently (library-list.tsx:118-120).
Preserve `q` when applying a tag filter by merging searchParams (page.tsx:39-42) — build `?q=..&tag=..`.

surfaces.composition: Landing (page.tsx): centered `min-h-[70vh] flex flex-col items-center justify-center gap-8` with an autofocus PsychSearch combobox (psych-search.tsx) and a single 'Browse by mechanism' link card. /learn (learn/page.tsx): `max-w-4xl space-y-8` where EVERY mechanism group renders fully expanded with all drug chips (`groups.map` + `flex flex-wrap gap-2`).
surfaces.primaryAction: Type a drug name to look it up (the one action). On the landing it IS dominant (autofocused single field) — this is the best existing phone-first pattern in the codebase. /learn has no primary action; it is a wall of fully-open groups.
violations: /learn dumps every mechanism group fully expanded with no collapse/accordion and no in-page search (learn/page.tsx:25-48) — dense, no progressive disclosure, one cognitive unit at a time is violated.
/learn drug chips are `flex flex-wrap` pills with no count-aware grouping or filtering (learn/page.tsx:32-45); finding one drug requires scanning the whole page.
Landing 'browse by mechanism' is a single monolithic card (page.tsx:24-38) that dumps the user into the un-scoped /learn wall rather than offering a progressive refine step.
PsychSearch has no debounce — it fetches on every keystroke (race-protected but not rate-limited, psych-search.tsx:38-60); fine on desktop, wasteful on a flaky mobile connection.
fixes: Convert /learn to an accordion (MobileSection + one open group at a time) so only one mechanism family is in view; add a live filter/search box at top to jump to a drug (learn/page.tsx:25-48).
Add a small debounce (~150ms) to the PsychSearch fetch to match the mobile-connection posture (psych-search.tsx:38-60).
Keep the landing single-field search as the canonical reference for the new mobile search primitive (it already does show→act→reveal: name → dose chips → band view).

surfaces.composition: Server-rendered list of ~100 medications (page.tsx) with a single name filter input (review-filter.tsx) that does `router.replace` on every keystroke, then a flat `space-y-2` list of cards with status badges. No MobileHeader; generic shell only.
surfaces.primaryAction: Open a medication to edit/review (the single per-row 'Open' link). The filter input is a secondary affordance but is autofocused on load (review-filter.tsx:14-16), which competes with the primary 'open' intent.
violations: Filter does `router.replace` per keystroke with no debounce (review-filter.tsx:18-24) — a full navigation storm on mobile and a performance bug.
No filter bottom sheet and no sort control; the only ordering is server-side `order('generic_name')` (page.tsx:40-43) — T37 sorting is entirely absent.
Filter input is `max-w-xl` inline with no accompanying active-state or clear affordance (review-filter.tsx:27-34).
fixes: Debounce the URL replace (~200ms) or move to local state + `router.replace` on commit (review-filter.tsx:18-24).
Add a sort control (A-Z / by status / by class) as a small segmented control or MobileBottomSheet, preserving the server list unchanged.
Wrap the page with MobileHeader; render rows as MobileListItem (generic_name + drug_class/status trailing) instead of the bespoke Link card (page.tsx:73-98).

surfaces.composition: Dense `<Table>` inside a bordered container (page.tsx:77-112) with Email/Expires/Signed-in columns plus a per-row actions cell. `Card` wrappers + PageHeader; no mobile primitives. No search, no filter, no sort.
surfaces.primaryAction: Add a student (CreateStudentForm at top). The table has no single action per screen; the 'Add a student' card competes with the roster table.
violations: Dense desktop table rendered unchanged on mobile — columns will cramp/overflow at 320-430px (page.tsx:77-112); pure CSS-shrunk desktop.
Zero search/filter/sort on a roster that grows unbounded (page.tsx:31-35) — T36 'search wherever available' is unmet.
No mobile list representation; MobileListItem exists (used only in courses/[courseId]) but is not applied here.
fixes: On mobile render the roster as MobileListItem rows (email + expiry subtitle + active-session StatusPill trailing) and reserve the table for lg+ (page.tsx:77-112).
Add a search field (filter by email) and a sort/filter by expiry or active-session, surfaced in a MobileBottomSheet, not an inline table header.

surfaces.composition: Status chips (All/Pending/Graded) as Links (page.tsx:89-109) + a second row of two native `<select>` dropdowns (course, assignment) + a 'Filter' submit button (page.tsx:112-142), then a `space-y-3` list of SubmissionReviewRow cards. No mobile primitives.
surfaces.primaryAction: Review pending submissions (the 'Pending' chip + count badge). Reasonable, but the filter chrome (two rows of controls) permanently consumes screen space before the list.
violations: Dense desktop filter panel: two `<select>` + submit permanently occupy space and are not progressive (page.tsx:112-142) — the exact T37 anti-pattern.
Status is a mix of URL Link chips and form selects — two different interaction models for the same filter, confusing on mobile.
No sort (by submitted date, lateness, student), so the list order is fixed to query order (page.tsx:28-37).
Course/assignment selects list ALL courses/assignments with no grouping or search inside the dropdown (page.tsx:119-137) — unwieldy on mobile.
fixes: Move course/assignment/status filters into a MobileBottomSheet with a sticky 'Apply' footer; surface active filters as removable chips + the pending count above the list (page.tsx:89-142).
Add a sort control (newest / oldest / late first) in the same sheet, preserved in URL params.
Keep the high-frequency 'Pending'/'Graded' as compact chips outside the sheet so the primary review action stays one tap away.

surfaces.composition: Summary count chips row (rights-list.tsx:178-197) + two inline `<select>` filters (status + layer, rights-list.tsx:200-227) + a `<table className='min-w-[960px]'>` wrapped in `overflow-x-auto` (rights-list.tsx:236-237). No mobile primitives.
surfaces.primaryAction: Set each title's rights status via a per-row `<select>` (rights-list.tsx:273-286). The 10-column table with forced 960px min-width is the dominant (and broken-on-mobile) layout.
violations: `min-w-[960px]` table forces horizontal panning on mobile (rights-list.tsx:236-237) — the hardest 'CSS-shrunk desktop' violation in this workstream.
Two inline `<select>` filters permanently consume space and are not progressive (rights-list.tsx:200-227).
Ten table columns (Title/Authors/Publisher/Category/Layer/Priority/Status/Consent/Unlocks/Updated) is far beyond a mobile cognitive unit.
Per-row status `<select>` is a desktop affordance; there is no mobile tap-target-friendly status changer.
fixes: On mobile render each title as a MobileCard / MobileListItem (title + authors subtitle + status StatusPill) with a 'Set status' action opening a MobileBottomSheet of status options, replacing the per-row `<select>` (rights-list.tsx:253-306).
Keep the 960px table only for lg+; the mobile list is the source of truth on small screens.
Move status + layer filters into a MobileBottomSheet with active-filter chips; keep the summary counts as a compact horizontal chip row (rights-list.tsx:178-197).

surfaces.composition: `mx-auto max-w-4xl px-4 py-8` list of lead cards (page.tsx:40-77), already card-per-row (good), but no search, no filter, no sort by status/source/date.
surfaces.primaryAction: Read/contact a lead (email link). Reasonable focus, but the list is unsorted and unsearchable as it grows.
violations: No search or filter on leads despite status (`STATUS_LABEL`) and source fields being available (page.tsx:17-38) — T36 'search wherever available' unmet.
List is a flat `space-y-3` with no status grouping or sort (page.tsx:51-76).
fixes: Add a search field (name/email) and a status/source filter in a MobileBottomSheet; group or sort by recency (page.tsx:51-76).
Optionally compose as MobileListItem with a StatusPill trailing.

surfaces.composition: command-palette.tsx renders a centered modal `fixed inset-0 ... pt-[12vh]` with a keyboard-driven list (↑↓/Enter/Esc). palette-trigger.tsx shows '⌘K' only via `hidden sm:inline` (line 19). palette-host.tsx feeds 40 case docs + static entries.
surfaces.primaryAction: Search and jump to a tool/course/case. On desktop it is fine; on mobile there is effectively no equivalent (no keyboard, no tap-optimized surface).
violations: Mobile has no full-screen phone search: the palette is a desktop modal (pt-[12vh], max-w-xl, keyboard ↑↓/Enter) that degrades on touch (command-palette.tsx:104-114, 139-179).
The trigger's only label is '⌘K' and it is `hidden sm:inline` (palette-trigger.tsx:19) — on mobile the search affordance is a bare icon with no discoverable gesture.
No filters or progressive refinement — results are one flat grouped list; tapping a case navigates to the library with a raw `?q=` prefix (palette-host.tsx:16) rather than an in-palette preview.
fixes: Add a mobile variant: on small screens render the palette as a full-screen search sheet (input at top, results as MobileListItem, tap-to-go) reusing the same searchPalette data; keep ⌘K/modal for lg+.
Make the mobile trigger a visible 'Search' bar/icon in the top bar (not `hidden sm:inline`), and support tap-driven selection.
Consider a result-detail preview (bottom sheet) for case hits instead of navigating directly.

sharedPrimitives: MobileSearchFlow — full-screen phone search (autofocus input, live/debounced results as MobileListItem, empty/loading states, tap-to-navigate); canonical reference is PsychSearch (psych-search.tsx).
MobileFilterSheet — a MobileBottomSheet specialization for filter panels: grouped option rows + a sticky 'Apply'/'Reset' footer; preserves every filter without consuming screen space.
MobileSortControl — a small segmented control or sheet for sort order (A-Z, newest, status) shared by psychopharm-review, submissions, students, enquiries.
MobileActiveFilters — a removable-chip row (StatusPill with an × affordance) that surfaces applied filters above any filtered list.
MobileResultDetail — a bottom-sheet detail view (snippet + note/hint + actions) so result rows stay single-tap and contextual tools are revealed progressively.

MobileListSearchAdapter — helper that maps a server/filtered list into MobileListItem rows and swaps desktop `<Table>`/card grids to mobile lists at the `lg` breakpoint (applies to students, rights, submissions).
priorities: Fix /admin/rights first: the `min-w-[960px]` table (rights-list.tsx:236-237) is the worst mobile break — convert to a MobileListItem card list with a bottom-sheet 'set status' and bottom-sheet filters, keeping the table for lg+.

Convert /practice/library into the canonical phone-first search: live search, bottom-sheet tag filters (replacing the 10-chip row at page.tsx:35-48), bottom-sheet notes (library-list.tsx:140-187), and load-more replacing the 50-cap (page.tsx:50).

fixes: Keep horizontal comparison ONLY because it is genuinely necessary here (drug vs drug at a dose), but restyle as a mobile compare: sticky left field-label column + per-drug horizontal scroll-snap, or a two-drug card with a field accordion.

sharedPrimitives: MobileRecordList — a generic stacked-record primitive that renders any table row as a scannable card (title + metadata line + trailing status/action), replacing the shadcn Table on students/rights/checkins/courses/idioms. Composes MobileListItem.
MobileMetricStrip — a horizontally scrollable row of metric chips (or 2-up grid) replacing the grid-cols-3/4 summary tiles on pulse/checkins/passport/Overview so no screen crams 3-4 equal stats.
MobileFilterSheet — a MobileBottomSheet that hosts filter selects/segmented controls, replacing the inline filter bars on submissions and rights.
MobileBulkActionBar — a sticky bottom bar + MobileBottomSheet hosting multi-select bulk actions (publish/schedule/grant/revoke) for modules, so the module list stays primary.

MobileProgressLine — a single compact progress affordance (bar OR 'N/M', never both + % + CTA) to standardize T40 course/lesson/assessment progress; used across dashboard course cards, passport, and completion states.
MobileCompareGrid — a comparison primitive for the genuinely-necessary horizontal drug comparison: sticky first column + scroll-snap columns, or a per-field accordion for 3+ drugs.
MobileDetailSheet — a reusable bottom sheet for record detail (rights title metadata, idiom edit, competency evidence, submission filter) so detail is revealed progressively instead of inline.

session-view.tsx:325-373 — the 'more' sheet nests two further sheets (Notes sheet opens after setMenuOpen(false); Hint sheet after setMenuOpen(false)) — a menu→sheet→sheet handoff is two stacked modal transitions for one task.

session-view.tsx:333-359 — 'Need a hint?' and 'Notes' are contextual but their trigger lives only behind the 'more' menu; there is no persistent affordance, so a first-time user can't discover the hint exists.

Move 'Need a hint?' and 'Notes' triggers out of 'more' into small contextual icon buttons in SimulationHeader (reuse the existing NotesSheet/HintSheet MobileBottomSheet) so the 'more' menu no longer needs to hand off into a second sheet.

Reduce the 'more' menu to only truly-rare actions, and keep the sheet→sheet handoff single: tapping Notes/Hint in 'more' should close the menu and open the target sheet in one visual step (already does), but ideally the triggers don't live in 'more' at all.

surfaces.primaryAction: There is no single primary action — 'browse/drag', 'Add a link', per-row ⋯, and per-row rename all compete. On touch, the drag-drop zone is a desktop affordance that cannot be triggered by drag.
violations: material-uploader.tsx:388-433 — 'Add a link' opens a centered Dialog (DialogContent line 395) with two fields; on mobile this should be a bottom sheet or inline expansion, not a centered modal.
material-uploader.tsx:559-584 — each material row's actions are a Radix DropdownMenu (floating desktop menu) instead of a mobile bottom-sheet action menu.
material-uploader.tsx:602-625 — delete confirm is a centered Dialog (line 603), not a bottom-sheet confirm.

material-uploader.tsx:344-384 — the primary input is an HTML5 drag-drop zone (onDragOver/onDrop); drag does not exist on touch, so mobile users only get the 'browse' click path — the affordance is desktop-shrunk.
fixes: Convert 'Add a link' from Dialog to a MobileBottomSheet (reuse src/components/mobile/mobile-bottom-sheet.tsx) with a title/URL form + pinned footer submit.
Replace the per-row DropdownMenu with a MobileListItem-style ⋯ trigger that opens a MobileBottomSheet action menu (Rename / Replace / Delete) — contextual actions revealed on demand.
Convert the delete confirm to a MobileBottomSheet (title 'Delete this material?' + destructive footer button), matching the pattern already established in notes-sheet/hint-sheet.
For touch: keep the 'browse' button as the single primary action and demote the drag-drop zone to a visual hint (or add an explicit 'Choose files' primary button); drag remains a desktop enhancement.

violations: course-actions.tsx:92-117 — unpublish confirm is a centered Dialog (line 93), not a bottom sheet.
course-actions.tsx:119-170 — delete confirm is a centered Dialog (line 143) nested inside/alongside a DropdownMenu trigger (line 134) — a dropdown → modal chain.
course-actions.tsx:120-141 — the ⋯ actions use Radix DropdownMenu (floating menu) instead of a mobile bottom-sheet action menu.
course-actions.tsx:80-89 — the Publish/'Set to draft' button is a permanent secondary control on every row, competing with the card title link for attention.

student-actions.tsx:67-92 — delete confirm is a centered Dialog (DialogContent line 73), not a bottom sheet.
student-actions.tsx:82-90 — DialogFooter stacks Cancel/Delete vertically on mobile (flex-col-reverse) inside a centered modal, taking over the small screen.

course/[courseId]/page.tsx:178-190 — every lesson row permanently shows Watch/Upload/Delete buttons (3 controls per row) instead of a single tap target with contextual actions.

surfaces.composition: ⌘K 'Ask the Syllabus' command palette: a fixed overlay anchored top (pt-[12vh]) with a centered max-w-xl card. Trigger is a button whose '⌘K' label is hidden on mobile (sm:inline).
surfaces.primaryAction: Search; it is desktop-first (keyboard-driven). On mobile there is no keyboard shortcut and the trigger text is hidden, so search is effectively undiscoverable on phones.
violations: command-palette.tsx:106 — the overlay is top-anchored with pt-[12vh] and a centered card, a desktop modal pattern, not a mobile bottom-sheet search.
palette-trigger.tsx:19 — the '⌘K' label is hidden on mobile (hidden sm:inline), leaving only a tiny icon; no accessible label is shown for touch users beyond aria-label/title.
fixes: Render the palette as a MobileBottomSheet on small screens (full-width search bar pinned above the keyboard) and keep the centered card only for desktop.
Give the trigger a visible 'Search' label on mobile (or add search to the mobile top bar / bottom tab bar) so the entry point is discoverable by touch.

surfaces.composition: Student course overview is already mobile-first: flat list of MobileListItem lessons grouped by week, one 'Start here' emphasis row, one 'My Courses' back link. Good example of the directive.
surfaces.primaryAction: The single 'Start here' next-action row (emphasis) is the one dominant action — correctly identified and highlighted.

sharedPrimitives: MobileActionSheet — a ⋯ (more-horizontal) trigger that opens a MobileBottomSheet list of contextual actions (Rename/Replace/Delete/Watch/Upload/Edit/Report), replacing every Radix DropdownMenu on mobile. Reuses MobileBottomSheet + MobileListItem.

MobileConfirmSheet — a destructive-confirm bottom sheet (title + warning description + pinned destructive footer + Cancel), replacing every centered confirm Dialog in student-actions/course-actions/material-uploader/delete-lesson-button/assignment-editor.

MobileStickyAction — a pinned bottom action bar (above safe-area) holding the ONE primary/terminal action per screen (e.g. 'Finish & debrief', 'Next lesson', 'Submit assignment', 'Send'), so the primary action is never buried in a menu.
MobileFormSheet — a bottom-sheet wrapper for short 2-3 field forms (Add a link, rename, quick create) with a pinned footer submit, replacing centered Dialogs that hold form fields.

MobileContextualToolbar — a compact set of contextual icon triggers (notes, hint, share, report, metadata) for the header of immersive surfaces (sim session, material viewer), so secondary tools are discoverable without a 'more' menu.
priorities: 1. Ship MobileStickyAction and lift 'Finish & debrief' out of the 'more' menu in session-view.tsx:362-370 — the flagship tool's terminal action must be visible, not buried (T43/T45, highest value).

2. Ship MobileConfirmSheet and convert all 6 destructive confirms (delete-lesson-button.tsx:43, student-actions.tsx:73, course-actions.tsx:143/93, material-uploader.tsx:603, assignment-editor.tsx:251) from centered Dialog to bottom sheet (T43).

items: T46 — Mobile multi-step state preservation: preserve partially completed assessments, forms, lessons, cases, simulations, reflections, and workflows when navigating backward, opening a sheet, changing orientation, or leaving the screen.
T47 — Mobile interruption recovery: handle call/app-switch/lock/network-loss/refresh/return-later; restore the correct task/context without forcing a restart.
T48 — Mobile offline experience: offline-capable flows, subtle offline states, local progress preservation, understandable recovery.

surfaces.composition: Full-screen patient chat: sticky header (back + name + difficulty + status pill + timer + more) -> transcript -> composer (voice toggle + input + send). Notes/hint/finish live in bottom sheets via the 'more' menu. Composition is already mobile-correct (one surface, one dominant action).
surfaces.primaryAction: Send your next question to the patient (composer is the always-visible dominant control). 'Finish & debrief' is correctly demoted to the 'more' sheet (session-view.tsx:362-370). Composition is fine; the gap is persistence.
violations: MSE notes + hypotheses are pure client useState (session-view.tsx:92-93), rendered in NotesSheet (notes-sheet.tsx:34-54), and NEVER persisted to DB or localStorage — lost on refresh/navigation/phone-lock. The sheet itself says the note 'is half the assessment' (notes-sheet.tsx:56-57).
Composer draft input is client-only useState (session-view.tsx:83) — a half-typed question is lost on interruption; there is no pagehide/visibilitychange flush anywhere in the component.

Timer counts from mount, not from server `started_at` (session-view.tsx:86, 104-110); the 12-min auto-finish (session-view.tsx:104, 120-126) resets to 0 on resume even though `started_at` is already loaded server-side (page.tsx:32).
hintUsedRef is a client ref (session-view.tsx:97, set at 338) — opening the hint then refreshing loses the flag, so the debrief (Bug 4 honesty) no longer reports hint use.

No offline handling: send() catches network errors and restores input (session-view.tsx:143-152) but there is no queue/retry; offline surfaces only a bare 'Network error.' string (session-view.tsx:207-209).
fixes: Persist mseNotes + hypotheses + composer draft to localStorage (keyed by sessionId, e.g. `sim:notes:<sessionId>`, `sim:draft:<sessionId>`) with a debounced autosave in session-view.tsx and a flush on `pagehide`/`visibilitychange(hidden)`; restore on mount alongside initialTurns.

Derive elapsed `seconds` from `started_at` (pass it from page.tsx:32 as a prop, or subtract Date.now() at mount) so the 12-min limit survives interruption; keep the ticking interval for live display only.
Persist hintUsed to the session server-side (add a column or reuse sim_sessions) so a refresh does not drop the honest hint flag.
Add a `navigator.onLine` + `pagehide` listener (a `useOffline` hook) to (a) show a quiet offline pill and (b) hold an unsent turn in an outbox for retry instead of discarding it.

surfaces.composition: Three-phase single-station flow: choose -> active (timer + optional voice transcript) -> self-assess checklist + global rating -> save. One station at a time, 'Station N' context kept visible.
surfaces.primaryAction: Currently 'I'm done — self-assess' (osce-station.tsx) drives the flow; it is the dominant action during the active phase. Composition is single-task and fine.
violations: All in-flight state is client-only useState (osce-station.tsx:12-23: stationIdx, phase, checked, selfGlobal, startedAt, spoken) — a mid-station refresh/lock/orientation change drops the spoken transcript + checklist + phase; only a completed attempt persists (buildOsceAttemptPayload, fired at the end).
The voice `spoken` transcript is captured via web speech but held only in React state (osce-station.tsx:23, 40-41) — no local persistence, so the spoken record vanishes on any interruption.
fixes: Introduce a MobileFlowState helper that snapshots {stationIdx, phase, checked, selfGlobal, spoken} to localStorage (keyed `osce:station`) on every change and restores on mount, so a mid-station session resumes exactly where it left off.
Autosave the spoken transcript into that same snapshot as it accumulates (stt.onResult), not only at the end.

surfaces.composition: One-question-at-a-time guided flow: pick -> immediate feedback + rationale -> Next. Compact 'Question n of m' progress line (quiz-check.tsx:93-99; judgment-arena.tsx:110).
surfaces.primaryAction: Pick an answer (single dominant action per step); 'Next question' appears only after reveal. Composition is correct progressive disclosure.
violations: Per-pick attempts persist fire-and-forget (quiz-check.tsx:56-60 -> /api/practice/quiz/attempt; judgment-arena.tsx:66-75 -> /api/practice/sct/attempt) but the in-flow POSITION does not: QuizCheck `current`/`answers`/`revealed` (quiz-check.tsx:25-28) and Judgment `idx`/`answered` (judgment-arena.tsx:32-33) are client-only — refresh restarts at question 1 and the 'n of m' context is lost.
Quiz attempt fetch failures are silently swallowed (.catch(() => {}), quiz-check.tsx:60) with no retry/outbox.
fixes: Add a shared MobileFlowState (localStorage) that persists {idx, answers, revealed} keyed by the item set id for QuizCheck and Judgment, restoring position + already-answered items on mount so 'Question 3 of 10' is honest across interruption.
Route quiz/sct attempts through an outbox queue that replays on reconnect (fixes the swallowed .catch).

surfaces.composition: Multi-stage drills: MSE stimulus tagging (mse-trainer.tsx), Decode multi-select meanings (decode-arena.tsx), Formulation 4-stage sort->narrative->diff (forge.tsx). Each is a focused single-task flow with stage context.
surfaces.primaryAction: Per-step pick/tag/place (e.g. tap a card to select). Composition is fine.
violations: No in-flow persistence: MSE `stimulusIdx`/`picked`/`moodIdx`/`describeText` (mse-trainer.tsx:15-20), Decode `idx`/`selected`/`revealed` (decode-arena.tsx:15-17), Formulation `attempt`/`narrative`/`stage` (forge.tsx:14-21) are all client-only useState.
Decode has NO persistence at all (no attempt route, no localStorage) — an interruption loses the whole session with no recovery.
Formulation persists only at stage 4 (forge.tsx:25-42, 192); the sort + narrative built in stages 1-3 are lost if interrupted before then.
fixes: Apply the same MobileFlowState snapshot per tool (keys mse:session, decode:session, formulation:session) restoring stage/idx/selections on mount.
Give Decode a minimal per-pick or per-set persistence so the product does not silently drop all progress.

surfaces.composition: Write form (prompt + textarea + mood chips + save) above the entries list. Single-task, already close to the mobile target.
surfaces.primaryAction: Save entry (the sole submit; disabled until content is non-empty).
violations: Draft autosave to localStorage is the ONE correct pattern in the app (journal-view.tsx:42-70) — but it saves only `content`, NOT the selected `mood` (journal-view.tsx:28, 55-70), so a mood choice is lost on refresh.
Draft restore uses setTimeout(...,0) (journal-view.tsx:43) which is race-prone; a synchronous read in an effect is more reliable.
fixes: Extend the draft payload to {content, mood} and restore both (journal-view.tsx:42-70). Generalize this into a shared `useDraft(key)` hook (the wall and submission forms need the identical pattern).

surfaces.composition: Composer (textarea + anonymous toggle + Post) above threaded posts with reactions + inline reply composers.
surfaces.primaryAction: Post to the wall (sole submit).
violations: Composer `content` + `anonymous`, and reply `replyText` + `replyAnon`, are pure client state (wall-view.tsx:43-51) — no autosave. A mid-post interruption/navigation/refresh loses the entire draft. Direct T46 gap.
Post failure shows a bare 'Network error.' (wall-view.tsx:78) with no queue/retry and no offline state.
Reaction/reply failures are silently swallowed (wall-view.tsx:120-122, 181-183) with optimistic state left applied and never reconciled.
fixes: Add `useDraft` autosave for the post composer and the open reply composer (keys wall:draft, wall:reply:<postId>), clearing on successful submit.
Add an offline status pill (reuse StatusPill warning tone) and an outbox that holds a failed post for retry on reconnect.

surfaces.composition: Tab bar (Watch/Materials/Assignment) is URL-driven (?tab=) and survives refresh (lesson-tabs.tsx:12-14). One forward action (Next lesson/Finish course, complete-button.tsx). Video player persists progress + pauses on tab-hide.
surfaces.primaryAction: Next lesson / Finish course — a single forward action (complete-button.tsx:40-60). Correct.
violations: Assignment SubmissionForm note + selected files are client-only (submission-form.tsx:98-99: `picked`, `note`) — a long note or chosen-but-unsubmitted files are lost on refresh/interruption; no draft autosave.
The 'Check what stuck' QuizCheck inside the lesson (page.tsx:231-249) inherits the in-flow-position loss described for QuizCheck.
fixes: Add `useDraft` autosave for the submission note (key submission:note:<assignmentId>) and clear on submit; note the file list cannot be stored (File handles) so at least warn on unload.
This surface already models the target: video progress ping + visibilitychange pause (video-player.tsx:444-458) is the reusable T47 pattern to lift into a shared helper for other flows.

surfaces.composition: One primary card (Resume session or Decode) + streak line + weak-spots banner + in-progress chain + quick/deep chips. Already the 'one thing next' hub.
surfaces.primaryAction: Resume your session (today/page.tsx:78-96) when an active sim exists — this is the correct recovery surface and it works, because sim turns persist server-side.
violations: No offline/network state anywhere on the hub: with no connectivity the page renders empty/error with no offline pill or 'you have a session to resume' fallback.
The 'Resume your session' affordance restores the transcript but not the session's notes/draft/timer (see consulting-room surface), so resume is partial.
fixes: Add an OfflineStatusPill (StatusPill warning tone + onPress details) in the shell/today so offline is subtle and explainable.
Fix the consulting-room notes/draft/timer persistence first so that 'Resume your session' restores the FULL context, not just the transcript.

sharedPrimitives: useDraft(key, value) — debounced localStorage autosave + restore + clear-on-success + pagehide flush. Generalizes the ONE working pattern (journal-view.tsx:42-70) to wall composer, submission note, sim notes/draft.
useOffline() — navigator.onLine + online/offline events + visibilitychange -> boolean; powers a shared OfflineStatusPill (wrap StatusPill warning tone + onPress reveal details).
MobileFlowState(key, snapshot) — persists/restores in-flow position (idx/answers/revealed/stage) for QuizCheck, Judgment, MSE, Decode, OSCE, Formulation so 'Question n of m' survives interruption.
SimSessionDraft(sessionId) — session-scoped notes (MSE/hypotheses) + composer draft + elapsed-time-from-started_at, restoring the full context behind /today's 'Resume your session'.
OutboxQueue — queues failed non-idempotent POSTs (wall post/reply, quiz/sct/osce attempts, sim turn) and replays on reconnect, replacing the silent .catch(() => {}) pattern.
priorities: Fix the consulting-room session first (highest value, flagship tool): persist MSE notes + hypotheses + composer draft + elapsed time from started_at (session-view.tsx:92-93, 83, 86), and persist hintUsed server-side (session-view.tsx:97) — this is what makes /today's 'Resume your session' actually restore full context.
Add useDraft autosave to the two highest-frequency data-loss surfaces: wall composer/reply (wall-view.tsx:43-51) and assignment submission note (submission-form.tsx:98-99).

Ship useOffline + OfflineStatusPill (built on StatusPill) and wire it into the sim header, wall, and today hub for a subtle, explainable offline state.
Add OutboxQueue for the fire-and-forget attempts (quiz-check.tsx:60, judgment-arena.tsx:75, forge.tsx:42) and the sim turn so transient network loss does not silently drop progress.
